lessons.problem: Clicking 'Edit Work' on SongDetailPage caused a 1–3 second UI freeze. The CreativeDrawer (1408 lines, multiple tRPC queries) was statically imported and mounted synchronously on the already-heavy SongDetailPage.
lessons.solution: Replaced static import with React.lazy() to code-split the CreativeDrawer into its own 78KB chunk. Wrapped setEditingSong() in startTransition() so React yields to the browser during mount. Added Suspense boundary with a gold spinner fallback.

lessons.problem: No prefers-reduced-motion support. All canvas animations, constellation effects, and CSS transitions fired for users who had explicitly requested stillness. Accessibility violation.
lessons.solution: Added global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule to index.css collapsing all transitions to 0.01ms. Created useReducedMotion() hook for JS-based animations. Wired hook into constellation switch canvas and harmonic-resonance animation.

lessons.problem: Custom buttons in PlayerBar, WorkListRow, and SupportCreatorDrawer had no keyboard focus ring. Keyboard navigation was broken for the entire player. Mouse/touch users never noticed but keyboard users were completely blocked.
lessons.solution: Added global focus-visible rule to index.css: gold (#C49A28) outline with 2px offset on all :focus-visible elements. Suppressed for mouse/touch via :focus:not(:focus-visible). Added aria-label to all WorkListRow action buttons.

lessons.problem: VerifyPage — the highest-intent screen (QR scan destination) — had zero creator information, zero support action, and zero link to the creator's profile. The page proved the work existed but said nothing about the person who made it. Violated doctrine questions: attribution, support, discoverability.
lessons.solution: Added CreatorPanel component to VerifyPage: avatar with gold border, creator name, handle, bio/origin statement, work origin story in gold pull quote, Support Creator button (opens SupportCreatorDrawer), View Profile link. Extended getSongByWitnessId to return bio, originStatement, stripeAccountStatus.

lessons.problem: CreatorProfilePage had a 'Send a Gift' button that only opened a tip amount input. No way to access monthly patronage, licensing, or follow from the profile header. Supporting a creator required navigating to individual works.
lessons.solution: Replaced 'Send a Gift' with 'Support Creator' button on both desktop and mobile profile headers. Button opens SupportCreatorDrawer with all 6 options: one-time support, monthly patronage, purchase, license, follow, view provenance.

lessons.problem: Feed/social language detected in multiple places: 'Activity Feed' in DashboardPage, 'Unsubscribed from creator feed' in CreatorProfilePage. These phrases position Living Nexus as a social media platform rather than a registry and archive.
lessons.solution: Replaced all feed/social language with cathedral doctrine language: 'Activity Feed' → 'Witness Activity', 'creator feed' → 'witness subscription'. Added DesignDriftScanner to detect future language drift automatically.

lessons.problem: CathedralDivider section headers used font-serif (generic) and text-2xl (Tailwind default) instead of the cathedral type system. The most prominent visual element on the Explore page was not using Cinzel or Cormorant Garamond.
lessons.solution: Updated CathedralDivider to use font-heading (Cinzel) for section title and font-editorial (Cormorant Garamond) for subtitle. Added global semantic type classes to index.css: .ln-page-title, .ln-section-header, .ln-body-copy, .ln-caption, .ln-overline, .ln-mono.

lessons.problem: WorkListRow action buttons (Save, Add to Collection, Support) used opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 — completely invisible to keyboard users and screen readers. Touch users on mobile never saw them because hover doesn't exist on touch.
lessons.solution: Changed to sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100 — always visible on mobile (no hover), hover-reveal only on desktop (sm: breakpoint). Added aria-label to all three buttons.

lessons.problem: The Edit Work button on SongDetailPage caused a UI freeze because the CreativeDrawer was synchronously imported and mounted. The issue was not the context split (which was correct) but the synchronous mount of a 1408-line component on an already-heavy page.
lessons.solution: Root cause: static import at the top of WorkEditorContext.tsx. Fix: React.lazy() + startTransition(). The drawer is now a separate 78KB chunk that loads asynchronously. The Suspense boundary shows a gold spinner during the first load, then the chunk is cached.

lessons.problem: Living Nexus had rich public audio and registry APIs but no native television surface. A browser-wrapper approach would have made the creator's attribution and immutable WID record difficult to navigate with a Roku remote and risked creating an independent, stale data model.
lessons.solution: Added a bounded, read-only Roku home projection from the existing public song records and a standalone SceneGraph/BrightScript package. The channel uses a Task node for HTTPS JSON loading and carries creator attribution, WID, registration time, optional testimony, and canonical verification links as immutable presentation fields.

lessons.problem: The managed development preview was intercepted by production Open Graph middleware and returned only the static SEO body. Separately, the cinematic entry used a fixed, clipped viewport that could hide controls behind mobile browser and device chrome.
lessons.solution: Bypassed Open Graph/static-body middleware in development so preview requests reach Vite, added an idempotent React refresh bootstrap safeguard, and made the cinematic surface use dynamic viewport sizing, safe-area spacing, and internal overflow for short mobile screens.

lessons.problem: The cinematic entry delayed returning visitors because its only completion action appeared after the process phase began. Keyboard and mobile users needed a visible bypass that did not require waiting for the timed sequence.
lessons.solution: Placed an immediate, safe-area-aware Skip Intro control on the splash. It uses the existing splash completion boundary, marks the session as seen, exposes a descriptive accessible name, and leaves the full cinematic experience available through the existing entry control.

lessons.problem: Draft and Publish registration could fail with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'charCodeAt')` when an incomplete or restored tone profile supplied a missing accent string while the client assembled its harmonic signature.
lessons.solution: Centralized harmonic-signature construction in the shared Loop registration contract. The helper preserves valid deterministic accents, supplies explicit three-slot fallbacks for incomplete legacy data, and prevents malformed display metadata from blocking creator-owned Draft or Publish actions.

lessons.problem: A contextual agent workspace can accidentally become a second chat owner, a hidden persistence channel, or an authority-escalation surface when it accepts free-form Agent payloads or lets contextual state trigger playback, provenance, commerce, or diary mutations.
lessons.solution: ADR-023 Phase 1 introduced strict versioned Work/Creator/Provenance/Explore/Now Playing references, rejected extra mutation-shaped fields, labelled Agent output as a suggestion, kept state in the PNA session only, and exposed only explicit Open, Verify, and user-initiated Play actions. The Context Canvas has no query, persistence, registry mutation, commerce, or diary behavior.

lessons.problem: The existing songsRouter is a critical compatibility façade across Work registration, Registry lookup, Explore, Player telemetry, collection behavior, media, and commerce. A broad router split would risk changing public procedure contracts or weakening creator/provenance custody before the target boundaries were proven.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Slice 1 extracted only the read-only duplicate hash lookup into lookupExistingWorkByFileHash while retaining the identical protected songs.checkDuplicate façade, Zod input, response shape, no-match/own-match/other-creator behavior, and caller identity source. Added focused behavior, authorization, no-side-effect, full-suite, type, route-smoke, and database custody checks. The pattern is internal-helper-first with compatibility facades; it does not authorize further router separation.

lessons.problem: Work preparation existed only as dispersed MusicEnvironment state. Any attempt to make the boundary explicit risked changing the JSON property order used by the current WID signature, changing the songs.upload payload, or introducing premature reseal/revision enforcement.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Slice 2 added a pure PreparedWorkRegistration client model, an exact-order WID payload serializer, and a registration-payload adapter. The existing generateWID crypto path, songs.upload contract, Draft/Published values, asset uploads, WID/provenance behavior, and post-registration behavior remain unchanged. Field classes are informational only. Focused tests prove byte-identical WID serialization and value/key-order-identical upload payloads; typecheck, full regression, refinement baseline, guest registration smokes, and zero-write custody checks passed.

lessons.problem: The Work lifecycle used status and isPublic as a synchronized public-projection invariant, but ordinary metadata mutation accepted status without synchronizing isPublic. Both CreativeDrawer and EditChapel exposed that path, producing the invalid but reachable Published/isPublic=false state. Public Explore/creator/guest Work readers excluded that state while canonical WID and Witness Registry readers still admitted it.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Publication State Integrity Repair removed status from ordinary songs.updateMetadata input and persistence. CreativeDrawer and EditChapel now save metadata first and call the existing owner-gated songs.updateStatus authority only when lifecycle selection changes. Dedicated transition authority retains publication gates and synchronizes isPublic through isPublicForSongStatus. Focused tests prove Draft→Published, Published→Unlisted, Unlisted→Published, Draft/Published metadata saves, and status rejection through metadata. Existing divergent rows were read-only verified and deliberately not repaired.

lessons.problem: Direct Published registration and later Draft→Published transition had parallel readiness gates that could drift. The direct registration path omitted the partial-rights ownership requirement while the dedicated status authority enforced it. A blocked creator could receive inconsistent reasons depending on when they tried to publish.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Song Publication Fix introduced one pure publication-readiness evaluator shared by direct songs.upload Published registration and the existing owner-gated updateSongStatus transition. The evaluator returns one explicit, creator-actionable message listing full rights/license, bound cover, creator name/handle, bio/origin, profile photo, and testimony requirements. Existing UI error paths surface that message; WID, schema, Registry/provenance, storage, Explore predicates, routes, and existing Work rows remain unchanged.

lessons.problem: The existing admin router is correctly role-gated but mixes read-only administration with broad operational and mutation powers, including raw configuration, billing, work moderation, user roles, and generation controls. Making its root page the platform Control Plane would blur authority boundaries and make later safe configuration work vulnerable to scope creep.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Admin Control Plane Stage 1 mounted a distinct adminControlPlane tRPC namespace whose procedures are all adminProcedure-gated queries. The new root /admin dashboard is limited to bounded health, a server-owned fixed route manifest, existing diagnostic links, and redacted existing action-log rows. Tests prove guest/non-admin server denial, zero mutation procedures, no page mutation hooks, a fixed manifest with no target input, and action-detail redaction. Existing specialized /admin/* routes remain intact and outside the new Control Plane.

lessons.problem: A useful administrative control room needs operational context, but generalized metrics, health, route discovery, and audit detail can easily become invented telemetry, an arbitrary crawler, a privacy leak, or a back door into the existing broad admin router.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Stage 2 keeps the Control Plane query-only. It counts only existing users, non-deleted songs, public Published songs, Draft songs, WIDs, provenance events, and collections; shows only bounded redacted existing admin activity; declares static route groups from active app routes; labels storage/build as not instrumented rather than guessing; and links existing specialized /admin surfaces without inheriting their authority. Audit area/result are transparent display derivations from existing action/target fields, not new persisted claims.

lessons.problem: The existing CinematicSplash carried the Living Nexus entrance ceremony through text, waveform, particles, and manual process cards, but did not use the supplied vault atmosphere. Adding cinematic media naively could create a second interactive surface, obscure Skip Intro and keyboard controls, impose motion on visitors who request stillness, or damage mobile readability through an uncontrolled crop. The first decorative implementation also over-occluded the dark supplied film with a broad veil, making the intended vault unreadable and making the pre-existing compact text hierarchy appear visually shifted.
lessons.solution: Added the supplied six-second dark-gold vault film only as a durable, muted, inline, metadata-preloaded, aria-hidden, pointer-events-none background behind the existing splash. The correction makes the film fully visible with bounded source luminance while replacing the blackout veil with a restrained edge/top-bottom scrim; contrast belongs to the local process card and text shadow, not a page-wide suppression layer. The logo, card title, supporting copy, waveform, and entry typography now use larger bounded token-backed hierarchy, while the centered symmetrical focal point remains safe on mobile. A live prefers-reduced-motion hook suppresses both film and particle motion while retaining the existing void/glow ceremony, visible Skip Intro, and keyboard/manual entry controls. The film changes no Work, WID, Registry, provenance, publication, or route behavior.

lessons.problem: The Keeper needed a repeatable front-page song that resumes between entrance ceremonies, loops indefinitely, starts audibly when the browser permits it, and still offers a reliable mute path. Storing the audio bytes in the database would blur the platform storage boundary, while assuming audible autoplay would fail on common browsers.
lessons.solution: Stored Vault of Gold as a durable webdev object and referenced its stable asset URL from a self-contained CinematicSplash audio controller. The controller restores local position, volume, and mute preference; targets a 40% default volume; loops without an end state; attempts audible playback and falls back to muted playback when autoplay is blocked; exposes explicit Unmute/Mute and range volume controls; persists progress; and pauses/removes the element on Skip or Archive exit. The track is entrance media only and does not become a Work, WID, provenance event, database record, or global player stream.

lessons.problem: A listener-started stream can survive ordinary page rendering yet still stop after a temporary media network interruption. Treating every media error as a next-track condition loses the listener's chosen Work and position; retrying every pause risks overriding an explicit Pause.
lessons.solution: Keep one app-wide audio owner and recover only the same current durable source after a recoverable network error or sustained stall. Preserve the last known position, use a finite 750ms/2s/5s retry budget, clear retry state on successful play, track/queue change, completion, or explicit Pause, and retain the existing Play control after exhaustion. Background stalls/errors use the same bounded policy rather than a competing reload path.

lessons.problem: A new AI-adjacent ingestion path could easily become an implicit registration, WID, publication, PNA-context, or provider pipeline if its worker writes directly into existing Work or provenance models. A process restart could also strand or duplicate background work if job state were held in memory.
lessons.solution: I1 establishes a Core-owned, additive Ingestion Commission with isolated Commission, job, and inspection-receipt tables; creator scope and idempotency; storage-verified audio inspection; deterministic hash/receipt evidence; optimistic durable job claims, finite retries, lease recovery, and scheduler-only execution. The initial procedures cannot create a Work, issue a WID, add provenance, publish, invoke a model/provider, access PNA/Quiver/avatar data, or activate a scheduler.

lessons.problem: A deterministic inspection receipt can be mistaken for authorization to create a canonical Work. A browser-side confirmation value can also become a durable secret or a replayable authority if it is displayed, stored as plaintext, insufficiently bound to a reviewed proposal, or valid indefinitely.
lessons.solution: I2 creates only creator-private review records: an exact receipt-and-asset-bound proposal, a 15-minute one-time confirmation whose SHA-256 digest is stored server-side and checked with constant-time comparison, and one private Commission Draft. The review page holds the opaque value only in page-session memory and does not render it. It provides no model/provider, scheduler, PNA, avatar, canonical Work, WID, provenance, or publication operation; later registration remains an explicit separate choice through the existing path.

lessons.problem: A technically correct creator-private Commission API is not usable when it requires a creator to know an opaque Commission identifier before selecting the audio they already own. Directly reusing a Work asset also risks silently mutating or reclassifying the canonical Work that stores it.
lessons.solution: Expose a creator-private selector that reads only the authenticated creator’s persisted audio rows with valid `audio/{creatorId}/` keys, then starts and attaches an I1 Commission through the existing idempotent boundaries. The source Work remains untouched. The interface labels the action as private preparation and states that no Work, WID, publication, or AI context changes. Queue processing stays separate: a scheduler plan requires a task-UID-bound configuration, deployed callback verification, explicit cadence choice, safe no-op pause, and a separate operational authorization before any schedule exists.

lessons.problem: A scheduler callback that recognizes only a generic cron identity can be reached by the wrong managed task, and an unauthenticated request that becomes a 500 can trigger wasteful retry behavior. A browser-facing or administrative mutation must not be able to create or silently enable a worker schedule while it is still undergoing deployment validation.
lessons.solution: Option B uses an isolated disabled-by-default scheduler singleton with a fixed five-minute cadence and callback path. The callback now requires both managed-cron identity and an exact bound task UID; unbound or disabled tasks return a successful no-op before worker execution, while direct unauthenticated requests return a non-retryable cron-only denial. Only an administrator may bind an already-created platform task, and that binding verifies the exact approved name, cadence, callback path, and method. Binding never creates, updates, or enables a task. Aggregate execution outcomes are retained without creator content, secrets, asset URLs, or canonical authority changes.

lessons.problem: A launcher can easily become a shadow navigation or audio system when it guesses product routes, creates its own audio engine, or treats a currently playing Work as available AI context. Copying a reviewed UI without preserving its declared route and ownership boundaries would fragment the Living Nexus surface.
lessons.solution: Treat the launcher as a presentation and handoff layer only. Declare every destination centrally; keep unavailable products visibly inert; retain user favorites as browser-local preference; delegate playback exclusively to the existing PlayerProvider and WSPProvider; and refresh an already-mounted Explore surface from its query string. The launcher never loads audio, edits the queue, issues a WID, creates provenance, or attaches AI context merely because the listener opens playback.

lessons.problem: An older theme patch can be visually useful while being structurally unsafe: direct application may overwrite later player, cinematic, responsive, launcher, and multi-theme work. Hard-coded gold, white, and near-black values also make a theme direction drift across Black Gold, Crimson, Illuminated Gold, and Parchment Cream.
lessons.solution: Treat historical theme work as art direction, not as patch authority. Introduce semantic atmosphere values derived from the current `--ln-*` palette, then port selected shared-chrome and route seams to those tokens. Protect audio/video/waveform mechanics, PlayerProvider/WSPProvider ownership, data queries, routing, mobile layout, and provenance behavior. Validate the existing protected contracts plus desktop/mobile screens before checkpointing.

lessons.problem: The onboarding router passed `completedSteps` as a JavaScript array into an `onboardingProgress.completedSteps` schema column intentionally defined as text. Drizzle/MySQL expanded that array into multiple SQL values during an update, causing TiDB syntax failure and preventing authenticated onboarding progress from saving.
lessons.solution: Keep the UI and router contract ergonomic (`string[]`), but normalize at the database boundary. `serializeOnboardingProgressPatch` converts arrays into one JSON text scalar before every insert or update, while preserving already-serialized text, null, and unrelated fields. This protects both creation and update paths without changing creator profile data, onboarding step semantics, Works, WIDs, provenance, player behavior, or Nexus boundaries.

lessons.problem: Onboarding previously advanced optimistically after invoking persistence, hid field requirements behind a disabled Continue control, and gave no truthful confirmation that a creator’s progress had reached the database. This made a failed update difficult to distinguish from a completed save.
lessons.solution: Validate the current step before the mutation, render accessible field-specific errors and focus the first invalid control, then disable the applicable submit action with a visible saving state while the mutation is pending. Advance the step and mark it complete only after `mutateAsync` resolves; show a success toast only then, and retain the current step with a recovery toast on failure. Optional testimony and license paths may deliberately skip validation rather than bypassing persistence safety.

lessons.problem: A visually compelling spatial prototype can still imply production authority when browser-local interactions simulate WID issuance, registration, witness records, playback/progress, AI context, creator identity, or asset generation. Committing large prototype media under application source also violates managed static-asset custody and deployment discipline.
lessons.solution: Retain the spatial-language principle while separating representation from authority. The current-source study uses neutral illustrative nodes, local orientation state only, semantic CSS/SVG geometry, and explicit no-read/no-write language. It contains no tRPC/auth/player/provider/Registry/PNA dependency, no audio/timer/file APIs, no WID-shaped fixture, no mock ceremony, no source-tree media, and gates all nonessential movement under reduced-motion preference. A real production projection requires its own Core/Registry read contract and canonical-player delegation approval.

lessons.problem: Public MusicRecording output mapped the system-created Work timestamp to `datePublished`, conflating platform record establishment or registration-adjacent time with a creator’s original release declaration. A public audit surfaced 639 affected public records, alongside separate Registry projection conflicts and missing creator/technical metadata that must not be fabricated.
lessons.solution: Render historical date semantics from their existing creator-controlled fields only: `releaseDate` becomes `dateCreated` and `creatorReleaseDate` becomes `datePublished`. Preserve the exact persisted calendar day, omit unknown declarations, and show the system record date under an explicitly different label. Keep WID as an identifier; do not rewrite a Work, backfill metadata, change a Registry record, or treat audit media enrichment as a data mutation. Handle duplicate WIDs, 404s, Registry/page mismatches, and missing metadata through separate governed diagnostics.

lessons.problem: Public discovery split basic Explore matching from canonical /search and rendered loading or failure states as thin text, making it difficult to recover from a failed request or express a multi-part discovery request.
lessons.solution: Extended the existing Explore and /search surfaces rather than introducing a parallel index. Explore now has explicit sort controls, in-place refresh, skeleton loading, and retryable Registry failure UI. /search adds an opt-in Keeper-guided interpreter that receives only the visitor phrase, returns visible bounded filters, and delegates all results to the existing public Registry search. Model failure falls back to deterministic parsing; no model generates Registry records, WIDs, or provenance claims.

lessons.problem: Work registration and placement editing persisted correctly but did not consistently invalidate existing owner Work and album projections. Separately, creator-only Explore still fetched the full multi-branch Work discovery payload and then requested like state it could not display.
lessons.solution: Centralized existing query invalidation at the successful registration and edit boundaries for Work lists, album lists, track lists, collection detail, available-track selectors, and Explore. Edit Chapel and Creative Drawer hydrate only clean forms from incoming Work data, preserve local unsaved edits, and reset when the Work identity changes. Explore now gates the Work feed and bulk-like request behind list view while creator browsing queries only the public creator projection.

lessons.problem: Explore requested up to 700 full Work records and repeated them in curated rows, creating a 13.6 MB response and 67,415-node document; playlist search queried the Registry on each keystroke; CreatorDomainShell eagerly read owner works and analytics.
lessons.solution: Moved the complete Works index to bounded cursor pages with explicit continuation, capped curated sections at 16, gated playlist Registry search behind a 300 ms current-query debounce, refreshed playlist list state after mutation, and deferred Domain work/analytics records until their sections open.

lessons.problem: Explore Registry order used a native select whose popup could inherit a light system surface while retaining light cathedral option text, making the active registry order difficult to read on mobile.
lessons.solution: Promoted the active Registry order control with cathedral gold and parchment contrast, set the native select color scheme to dark, and explicitly styled option surfaces. Audited database release readiness separately; recent schema objects exist in the live database, but SQL migrations 0134–0142 are absent from Drizzle journal metadata and require reconciliation before a reproducible public release.

lessons.problem: The Loop registration gateway and music environment treated canonical audio and artwork as unrelated layouts, creating a duplicate-feeling ingest, uneven spacing, and the inaccurate phrase bound visual.
lessons.solution: Introduced one RegistrationAssetCard grammar across gateway, canonical audio, and visual identity sections; made the in-memory audio handoff explicit; standardized type roles and touch targets; and clarified that visual identity is attached to the Work, required for public publication, but not part of the WID hash.

lessons.problem: The newly shared Manifest asset card did not explicitly differentiate desktop hover feedback from touch behavior or prove the readability of Work-to-visual relationship language on a dark surface.
lessons.solution: Reduced mobile card gutters while preserving full-width actions, gated artwork hover and focus-within feedback behind fine-pointer media queries, honored reduced motion, and moved relationship/support text to high-contrast cathedral tokens. Calculated contrast against the void: bone 11.59:1, parchment 15.82:1, gold 8.00:1.

lessons.problem: Loop inspected embedded music metadata but did not consistently promote verified ISRC, industry artist, album, publisher, and original release evidence into canonical Work fields before sealing.
lessons.solution: Added a creator-confirmed Detected Record review that prefills only blank fields, maps artist/album/ISRC/date to existing Work metadata, records publisher as a structured Work credit, and gates WID sealing on review without expanding the WID payload.

lessons.problem: Auto-extracted registration values were indistinguishable from creator-entered values, and creators could not quickly affirm a valid detected record or understand ISRC and release-date requirements before sealing.
lessons.solution: Added source-preserving Extracted markers, an Approve All acknowledgement gated by inline ISRC and chronology validation, tooltip explanations, and WID seal guards. Source markers clear when a creator or workspace changes the value.

lessons.problem: A multi-file audio selection could accidentally be treated as one provenance claim or allow a source type label to substitute for evidence before storage.
lessons.solution: Loop uses a bounded browser-memory MP3 queue, preserves one review and seal path per Work, and verifies marked queue sources as MPEG audio at the upload boundary.

lessons.problem: Creators could arrange a local MP3 queue but could not audition a selected source, set a clear pre-review Work-title proposal, or reset a mistaken selection without removing records one by one.
lessons.solution: Added local object-URL previews, a visible review-title input that only pre-fills the canonical title field, and a Clear all action that revokes browser-only preview URLs. The source filename, bytes, metadata review, disclosure, attestation, and per-Work WID path remain intact.

lessons.problem: The local MP3 Queue preview could start and stop audio, but it did not expose playback position, allow creators to scrub a selected source, support low-friction keyboard review, or show whether a proposed Work title diverged from source evidence.
lessons.solution: Added a browser-only preview progress range with elapsed/duration feedback and seeking, queue-scoped Space and arrow shortcuts that exclude editable and interactive controls, and title-origin labels. Playback state, proposed title, and queue selection remain local; no source bytes, evidence hash, disclosure, WID, server state, or global player queue is changed.

lessons.problem: A creator could arrange and preview an MP3 queue, but setting shared artist or album metadata still required retyping it in every sequential Work review. Arrow-key selection also lacked a visually unmistakable location.
lessons.solution: Added a browser-memory artist and album proposal that pre-fills only unstarted per-Work reviews, remains editable there, and does not alter source tags, hashes, completed records, disclosures, or WIDs. Added a persistent gold selection ring and Active label to the arrow-key-selected queue card.

lessons.problem: Batch queue review could propose artist and album metadata but required duplicate publisher and Original Release Date entry even when those values were shared. The permanence path needed evidence that bulk review does not become a bulk persistence bypass.
lessons.solution: Extended the local queue proposal to publisher and Original Release Date. Each unstarted MusicEnvironment review pre-fills the values but remains individually editable and subject to client/server chronology checks. Publisher travels through the established bounded Work-credit mapping; Original Release Date persists through the established creator-date field and append-only declaration event. Neither value enters WID serialization.

lessons.problem: A queued Work could inherit creator-proposed shared metadata from a bulk edit, but the individual Loop player did not disclose that provenance. This could make a bulk-prefilled value look indistinguishable from embedded-file extraction.
lessons.solution: Added an accessible, gold Bulk edit proposal panel to the individual queued Work player. It lists only the fields supplied by the local queue proposal and states they remain editable before sealing. The presentation explicitly distinguishes creator-proposed prefill from the existing Extracted marker for audio-file evidence and reiterates that no source metadata or WID boundary changes.

lessons.problem: The active Loop multi-Work registration could inherit an outer page scroll position and render a site footer within the review canvas. At 100% desktop zoom, that clipped the Studio header and compressed the asset typography.
lessons.solution: Made /manifest a contained workspace inside the existing application viewport. MainLayout now suppresses the document footer only for the Manifest route, StudioShell inherits its height and gives each panel independent scrolling, queue transitions reset the workspace to its own opening hierarchy, and the asset grammar uses a wider editorial measure with expanded type and spacing.

lessons.problem: Explore creator cards discarded creator banner imagery and allowed variable visual hierarchy despite an existing public bannerUrl projection.
lessons.solution: Mapped existing bannerUrl into the Explore creator summary, preserved profile photos as avatars, added an optional presentation scrim and fixed 5:4 card geometry with clamped statements and anchored actions, without changing support fetches or registry data.

lessons.problem: Creator discovery needed stronger browse feedback, a domain-specific discovery prompt, and stable loading affordances without changing the public creator query or loading every creator Work.
lessons.solution: Added a reduced-motion-safe 1.2% hover scale and shadow, switched the shared discovery field to creator-specific name/handle/statement filtering in creator mode, and introduced fixed-geometry directory plus image-level skeleton states.

lessons.problem: The Explore creator-card Witness action created a persisted subscription relationship without explaining that it preserves an ongoing relationship to a creator’s registered record. The profile command center also had no distinct view of those subscription-backed relationships.
lessons.solution: Added a concise Explore tooltip distinguishing Witnessing from a social follow, a protected subscription-backed creator directory, and a dedicated Profile Witnessing tab. The tab is intentionally separate from the legacy Witness Network so the two relationship systems are not conflated.

lessons.problem: Explore creator cards only expressed an established witness subscription inside the action button, making the current viewer relationship easy to miss during directory scanning.
lessons.solution: Added a non-interactive, token-based WITNESSING badge that derives directly from the existing followTier. It appears for every persisted tier without asserting a tier privilege or creating a new relationship source.

lessons.problem: The PNA private workspace had owner-scoped threads, private visual proposals, and a contextual Work panel, but those capabilities were difficult to discover and the context panel vanished below ultra-wide widths. Mobile risked inheriting a squeezed desktop workspace.
lessons.solution: Reused the existing cmdk, pnaThread.list, NexusContextPanel, and private Quiver proposal flow to add a keyboard-first command palette, inspectable Context and Artifacts rail, and a 44px mobile Conversation/Context/Artifacts switch. The implementation preserves explicit save-to-Quiver consent and adds no Registry, WID, provider, or publication authority.

lessons.problem: PNA threads and private Quiver proposals existed, but a creator could not inspect or revoke the exact selected context sent to a model route, profile permissions were not surfaced as a creator setting, and generated visuals could be saved without a governed review lifecycle.
lessons.solution: Added creator-private Context Envelopes with owner and revision checks, explicit remote selected-context consent per Stewardship Profile, immutable source-use and action receipts, and an Artifact Review lifecycle. Vision output enters a draft Artifact; only an explicit review then Preserve privately produces a Quiver copy. The implementation does not create Works, WIDs, testimony, provenance events, publication, licenses, payments, or public sharing.

lessons.problem: A PNA thread with deliberately attached Context sources could reject an ordinary Guide reply when remote selected-context permission was off. The server safeguard was correct, but the client attempted remote preparation whenever sources existed, contradicting the visible local-only state.
lessons.solution: PNA now sends a normal thread reply without forwarding attached sources until the active Stewardship Profile explicitly permits remote selected-context use. The composer states that attached context remains private, offers an explicit permissions handoff, and server-side owner/profile/envelope checks remain mandatory whenever remote use is actually authorized.

lessons.problem: The main-domain /pna route rendered inside MainLayout while the pna subdomain rendered the workspace directly. This caused duplicate public chrome and playback ownership, and the automatic What's New overlay could cover a creator's private workspace.
lessons.solution: Introduced one PNAServiceRouter and PNAServiceFrame for both PNA entry paths and the Stewardship route. The focused service boundary suppresses public release, assistant, upload, and PWA overlays; preserves an internal validated return path to the active thread; and leaves Registry/WID, message, model, and artifact authority unchanged.

lessons.problem: Creator-domain Work actions were split across implementation surfaces: a legacy profile component received card controls while the public /creator/:id route used LoopCreatorPage and SanctuaryWorksOrganizer. Separately, #voices deep-links could run before the asynchronous Work page had rendered the Voices landmark, leaving the hash set while the reader remained at the hero.
lessons.solution: Mapped the active public route before finalizing UI work. Creator Work rows now use one reusable, permission-aware quick-action group for hearts, playlists, and permitted WID-tagged downloads; heart state is loaded through the bounded existing bulk-status read. The Voices deep-link retries after Work hydration, so Signal alerts land at the conversation rather than only preserving the hash. Reading tiers and control targets were raised without changing authorship, WID, participation, or download authority.

lessons.problem: Model-assisted features were represented in several interfaces and services, so hiding PNA alone would still leave model, image, transcription, and automated visual paths callable.
lessons.solution: Introduced one disabled shared AI operations contract that blocks model provider calls before fetch; made transcription return an explicit paused result before reading creator media; skipped the AI music-video follow-on without changing Work status; and made PNA visibly work-in-progress with a read-only composer while private threads, Context Envelope, and Artifact review remain available.

lessons.problem: A global provider pause can be technically effective while legacy or secondary PNA surfaces still advertise actionable model controls, which weakens creator trust and can create unnecessary rejected requests.
lessons.solution: Audited the checkpoint for direct provider bypasses and retained the guarded adapter boundary. Added one shared pause notice to thread navigation, the command palette, inspection rail, legacy drawer, and Stewardship settings; disabled legacy compose and profile-permission controls before mutation while keeping private records reviewable.

lessons.problem: Four regression contracts treated intentionally archived pre-0134 Drizzle SQL as active files, masking a reconciled migration lineage with false missing-file failures. Work shortcuts also differed by song-tile surface, forcing repeated implementation and making download access inconsistent.
lessons.solution: Kept archived SQL out of the active journal, moved the affected contracts to inspect the preserved archive while asserting obsolete active paths remain absent, and extended lineage coverage. Reused one permission-aware Work action group in active creator rows, Explore cards and list rows, and Store tiles; it omits unavailable downloads and preserves existing heart, playlist, and tagged-download authority.

lessons.problem: A request to preserve a deceased creator's legacy could be implemented as a global administrator promotion or account transfer, either of which would blur creator identity and create unrelated platform authority.
lessons.solution: Used one creator/steward-scoped, revocable Legacy Stewardship grant with server-enforced scope checks, an append-only custody ledger, immutable steward-attributed memorial records, and a read-only Work/WID reconciliation digest. The public Creator Domain renders memorials separately from creator testimony and Work provenance.

lessons.problem: A Creator catalog inside a cinematic player can accidentally make browsing appear to change playback, can fetch an unbounded catalog, or can visually replace the actual listening Work without explaining that audio continues.
lessons.solution: Kept cinematic selection as local presentation state over the existing PlayerContext session, made Play the only queue-changing action, labeled Previewing and Listening now independently, added a return-to-listening action, cursor paging with duplicate Work-ID suppression, and browser-verified mobile horizontal catalog behavior.

lessons.problem: Stripe Connect entry points were scattered across Profile, Dashboard, Creator Domain, payment settings, and guide-upload surfaces. Several launched hosted onboarding directly, and the onboarding callback origin was not constrained to the platform's canonical payout route.
lessons.solution: Created one Creator Payouts center at /settings/payouts. All existing creator prompts now route there; only that page owns the browser-side onboarding mutation. The server accepts an origin only when it exactly matches the configured production or trusted preview origin, and both Stripe refresh and return URLs resolve to the server-owned payout route. Ready accounts render a confirmed, non-relaunching state.

lessons.problem: Public Creator Domains, Related Works, and Explore creator cards relied on implicit grid tracks or one-row action budgets while a fixed mobile header and mini player used mismatched safe-area reservations. Narrow devices could clip card content, make actions unreachable, or let fixed chrome obscure the last content.
lessons.solution: Applied local mobile-first containment before shared geometry: explicit Related Works tracks, a two-row Creator Domain action fallback, creator-card footer reflow, and local wrapping for dynamic values. Consolidated header, scroller, mini-player, and mobile rail reservations with shared safe-area tokens; secondary header controls collapse on narrow screens while Compose stays reachable in the mobile rail. Preserved PlayerContext, queue, WID, provenance, routes, and relationship authority.

lessons.problem: A published Work participation declaration was WID-bound at original registration but had no creator-authorized correction path; Collection Studio also could render guest denial before auth hydration and offered no bounded primary-request recovery. A reported playback-linked freeze remained observational rather than proven.
lessons.solution: Separated current effective participation disclosure from original WID evidence: owner-only no-op-rejecting corrections now update only the three effective axes and append before/after evidence atomically in one Work-event transaction. Studio now resolves auth before access UI, offers same-collection Retry and context-preserving Back, while PlayerContext and queue are untouched until playback causality is profiled.

lessons.problem: The PWA update banner could appear after an initial uncontrolled tab had gained its first service-worker controller, but update reload logic relied on a hadController snapshot captured only at startup. A listener-selected waiting update could therefore activate without reloading, while the banner provided no progress, failure, or retry state.
lessons.solution: Bound update application to explicit listener consent rather than startup controller state. The banner now requests a central one-shot activation handshake, announces Updating while duplicate clicks are blocked, and remains actionable with Retry after a bounded failure. Bootstrap reloads exactly once only after a consented controller change; initial clients.claim remains reload-free. Cache strategy and listener-approved SKIP_WAITING remain intact.

lessons.problem: Global Player Voices retained a listener draft while deriving its query, drawer header, and submission Work from the moving PlayerContext track. Automatic advance or a manual skip could therefore retarget an unfinished comment without listener action. The server accepted caller-supplied Work IDs before resolving public availability, and replies did not prove parent/Work coherence.
lessons.solution: Capture a stable canonical Work snapshot when the player composer opens, retain drafts keyed by Work ID, and permit target change only through an explicit Switch to Current Track action. Resolve public/published target availability before every list or write, and reject reply parents from another Work before side effects. Keep route-bound Work Voices and PlayerContext queue authority independent.

lessons.problem: The canonical public Creator Domain intentionally abbreviated its hero synopsis but had no full creator biography path. The underlying public profile query already returned the existing bio, while card excerpts were intentionally compact.
lessons.solution: Preserve the hero synopsis and card clamps; add one optional, semantic full Biography section to the canonical Creator Domain after metrics and before Testimonies. Render the existing plain-text bio with pre-wrap and local overflow containment, so creator-authored line breaks survive without duplicating data or changing schema, routes, provenance, or cards.

lessons.problem: Living Nexus needed a discoverable Provenance Player entry without implying account connection, WID verification, track authorization, shared playback, or a second audio authority. The existing cinematic entry is desktop-only, so adding a link only to desktop/cinematic controls would leave the companion unavailable from the actual mobile expanded-player surface.
lessons.solution: Use static target=_blank noopener anchors to one fixed external URL in the desktop action dock, cinematic panel, and reachable mobile expanded section. Keep the disclosure identical on each surface, add token-based visible focus styling and reduced-motion-safe transitions, and prohibit all onClick, navigation, PlayerContext, queue, Work, WID, account, or registry data handoffs. Validate the mobile entry at 375px with containment and target-attribute checks.

lessons.problem: A manual manifest bridge to the separate Provenance Player could expose raw media URLs, bypass public-state or individual-withdrawal changes, emit a misleading partial album/playlist, or treat a WID share URL as canonical despite duplicate Work identities. A preliminary per-Work external-display/free-download gate also contradicted the creator community’s approved-product policy and made existing public catalogs unusable.
lessons.solution: Build manifest JSON only through owner-authorized, bounded server projections that preserve canonical list order and fail closed for private, unpublished, flagged, malformed, individually withdrawn, or duplicate-WID members. Community approval supplies the initial availability rule; individual withdrawal remains an explicit creator safeguard. Put only a revocable Living Nexus media gateway in audioUrl so every fetch rechecks current eligibility. Keep copy/download local to the owner surface and independent from PlayerContext, queues, account sync, automatic external launch, and registry mutation.

lessons.problem: Legacy WID-ALB collections permitted current membership changes after their collective hash and WID were issued, while public routes could disclose private membership and named-playlist operations trusted unscoped row or Work IDs. That risked false current provenance claims and cross-container relationship changes without changing the historical record.
lessons.solution: Treat WID-ALB as an immutable origin membership seal. Replay its historical sorted-WID SHA-256 algorithm at every trust-bearing current-composition boundary; fail closed for public detail, verification, certificates, companion manifests, and ZIP exports on mismatch; preserve only presentation edits and same-member ordering. Bind playlist mutation to membership-row IDs, exact-set validation, container predicates, and one transaction. Defer changed membership to an explicit future edition, never hash/WID overwrite.

lessons.problem: Creators needed one relationship-first Collections surface for arranging existing registered Works, but legacy WID-ALB records are immutable origin-membership seals and the approved WID-ALB2 edition identity cannot be issued safely until the creator signing-key lifecycle is security-reviewed.
lessons.solution: Add a separate owner-private Draft Release domain with scoped draft membership rows, optimistic revisions, and append-only revision snapshots; route Creator Domain and Archive entry points to one workspace; keep legacy sealed albums presentation-only and named playlists in their one canonical editor. Apply only additive schema changes. Hold all WID-ALB2 sealing, publication, verifier, and Draft manifest export behind a truthful signing-readiness response rather than manufacturing an unsigned certificate.

lessons.problem: A public legacy WID-ALB whose current Work membership no longer reproduced its stored collective hash correctly failed at its canonical album route, but broad Creator Domain projections could still advertise the unresolved album and gave its owner no single relationship-first recovery path.
lessons.solution: Keep the historical WID-ALB fail-closed. Reuse the exact composition-seal replay in the shared public Creator Domain album reader; give only the owner a transactional action that snapshots the current eligible Works into a separate private Draft Release with observational legacy lineage. Never update legacy membership, collective hash, certificate, Work WIDs, media, HAAI declarations, or companion-player authority.

lessons.problem: Draft Release creation assumed that an insert executed through a MySQL transaction returns a direct ResultSetHeader. The transaction returned a tuple, so reading result.insertId yielded NaN and the related draft insert failed before any creator-visible draft could be created.
lessons.solution: Centralize transaction insert-ID normalization in a fail-closed helper that accepts direct and tuple-shaped MySQL responses, rejects invalid IDs before related writes, and maps that impossible persistence state to a clear retry-safe creator message. Apply it to both fresh and legacy-derived Draft Release creation paths.

lessons.problem: Owners could export approved Provenance Player manifests for their named playlists and albums, but had no equivalent manifest action at the canonical individual Work surface. This forced a creator to assemble or recover a one-track payload outside the Work they intended to carry into the companion player.
lessons.solution: Reuse the existing protected manifest adapter and revocable Living Nexus media gateway for a one-Work export. Require current Work ownership server-side, keep the actual WID and canonical share source, exclude raw storage URLs, and provide only copy/download JSON controls that leave the existing PlayerContext queue untouched. Test direct gateway authorization and failure cases independently from the UI.

lessons.problem: Creator workflows lived across several same-origin routes, while the dormant Creator Studio route was not a usable supported product boundary. Moving immediately to a separate origin would duplicate or broaden authorization, session, API, database, and playback responsibilities before the private authoring boundary was proven.
lessons.solution: Create a lazy same-origin /studio hub that composes only existing owner-authorized routes and read models: canonical registration, Creator Domain identity, current Work editing through WorkEditorContext, Collections, Archive export, payouts, and the external companion player. Keep the existing Living Nexus backend, session, database, WID/registry policy, media authority, and single PlayerContext untouched. Do not activate WID-ALB2 signing or create a separate Studio origin until its separate security gates are approved.

lessons.problem: The protected individual-Work Provenance Player exporter existed only in the unreachable legacy SongDetailPage, so the canonical /song/:id Work surface offered no portable manifest action while a second UI definition risked drifting from the actual routed experience.
lessons.solution: Relocate the existing owner-authorized Copy/Download controls to LoopWorkPage Chain of record beside WID and Verify; reuse the protected Work procedure and shared serialization helpers; keep manifest actions separate from PlayerContext; remove the inactive duplicate; and add a byte-parity contract for clipboard and .json output.

lessons.problem: The Provenance Player duplicate-WID guard counted Deleted historical Work rows as current identity collisions. This correctly preserved the history but incorrectly blocked a public successor Work from exporting and playing through the revocable gateway.
lessons.solution: Define manifest ambiguity across non-Deleted current rows only. Preserve every Deleted historical Work, its WID, media reference, and evidence untouched, but exclude it from current portable-delegation ambiguity. Continue to reject two or more non-Deleted rows sharing a WID; use the same helper for export and gateway rechecks.

lessons.problem: The individual Work Portable Witness exporter was limited to the Work owner even though the creator community approved eligible public Work portability as a discoverable companion-player experience. This hid the canonical action from listeners and blocked cross-creator manifest access unnecessarily.
lessons.solution: Make only the individual Work living-nexus-player/1 projection public. The canonical Work surface shows the existing Copy/Download controls to visitors with a WID, while a public server procedure still enforces published public audio, unflagged status, valid Creator attribution, clean HTTPS media, current non-ambiguous WID, and no companion withdrawal. Keep playlists and albums owner-controlled, preserve gateway-only audio with rechecks/no-store, and never touch PlayerContext or queues.

lessons.problem: The public Witness Registry exposed only a newest-first 50-record page. Creators, Works, and WIDs outside that initial page were not directly findable, encouraging duplicate discovery surfaces or browser-only filtering that could not reach the full ledger.
lessons.solution: Extend the existing public cursor-paginated Witness Registry procedure with a bounded optional query. Search the existing published WID projection by Work title, Witness ID, Creator name, and Creator handle (accepting a display-style @ prefix), reset pagination on a new query, debounce the responsive input, and retain the same canonical /song, /creator, and /verify links. No separate ledger, manifest store, schema, registry record, or playback authority is introduced.

lessons.problem: On narrow browser viewports, Living Nexus navigation remained a 72px icon rail with no coordinated dismissal lifecycle, while an independently fixed Global Player sheet could compete with it. The result was cramped navigation, page interaction behind the menu, and unreliable Android Back/Escape behavior.
lessons.solution: Keep LeftRail as the one navigation authority and place mobile presentation lifecycle in MainLayout: a readable focus-managed off-canvas drawer, one shared layer registry, main-scroll isolation, Escape and same-URL history dismissal, and a player-collapse event without changing PlayerContext or queues. Track visualViewport height in the existing GlobalPlayer so its expanded sheet remains inside the visible mobile browser viewport. Future native clients should preserve these contracts but replace DOM history, inert/focus, visualViewport, and CSS safe-area primitives with their platform-native equivalents.

lessons.problem: The first mobile-shell stabilization established drawer lifecycle and player coordination, but real 360px inspection still showed Creator Domain art and typography bleeding through the mobile drawer because the shared rail surface token retained transparency. The same pass also exposed a literal unfinished creator prompt in public narrative fields and narrow layouts that needed stronger summary-fact containment.
lessons.solution: Use one shared solid mobile drawer vessel over the existing capped backdrop, not a second navigation system or page-specific override. Retain the one LeftRail authority, MainLayout focus/Back/Escape lifecycle, and GlobalPlayer/PlayerContext ownership. Filter only known incomplete authoring prompts at render time, retain authored testimony, and render Who/What/When/Why as narrow-safe facts with wrapped actions. Validate a true 360px DevTools pass for zero horizontal overflow, drawer focus return, closed off-canvas state, and player coexistence before checkpointing.

lessons.problem: External media clients could use the legacy public catalog and raw stream redirect, which did not guarantee Portable Witness eligibility, current WID uniqueness, creator attribution, revocation handling, or gateway-only media. Jellyfin 12.2 also requires plug-ins to register IChannel through its service collection; an assembly that merely implements IChannel is not discoverable.
lessons.solution: Add a separate no-store companion catalog that derives each entry through the existing living-nexus-player/1 eligibility adapter, excludes ambiguous active WIDs, preserves stable pagination, and emits only the existing revocable provenance-player gateway URL. Package a Jellyfin 12.2 IChannel plug-in that accepts only that schema and host/gateway path, then register it through IPluginServiceRegistrator as a singleton IChannel. Validate a disposable host registration; do not publish a repository manifest until an immutable hosted ZIP download URL and its checksum can be verified.

lessons.problem: The Jellyfin 12.2 channel correctly preserved the revocable Living Nexus gateway but returned remote MediaSourceInfo without a declared container or Audio stream. Jellyfin Web therefore could not select an audio stream and failed before fetching the gateway. The catalog has no authoritative format field and includes at least one WAV object, so fixed MP3 metadata would have fabricated a media claim.
lessons.solution: Keep the gateway as the sole playback path. For each channel candidate, make a bounded 16-byte HTTPS range request with concurrency capped at eight; accept a direct MPEG frame or an ID3v2 header only when the transiently resolved object path ends in .mp3. Discard response bytes and resolved URLs, emit complete MP3/Audio MediaSourceInfo only for verified sources, and omit non-MP3 candidates. Validate a fresh Jellyfin 12.2 host through catalog discovery, gateway-only PlaybackInfo, browser playback, pause/resume/seek, and fail-closed media regression tests.

lessons.problem: HarmonicBar used a click-only custom div slider with no keyboard operation, no native control semantics, a compact hit area, and potential disagreement between controlled progress, visual time, and accessibility state.
lessons.solution: Replaced the interactive branch with a 44px native range target whose decorative harmonic line remains aria-hidden. One finite-safe normalized progress contract now drives native change, keyboard emissions, fill, playhead, and spoken time. A focused JSDOM slice protects precision, key behavior, static-branch inertia, and accessibility ownership; real-browser smoke verifies focus, zoom, and reduced-motion hooks.
